results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 55 outliner summaries match the controlling ideas of p01-p55 in the spec's order (scene, concepts, interference, designs, metrics, ranking-prices, architecture, practice, judging sections, conclusion); the five callouts match no spec paragraph, as expected.

results.draft_locus: Concepts: What an Experiment Must Get Right ¶2
results.quote: is the moment a unit encounters the treatment, which is often much later than assignment
results.finding: The outliner needed two summaries (primary metric chosen before the test / exposure as the moment a unit meets the treatment). The two definitions share no idea beyond 'two further terms', and the spec's p12 controlling idea joins them with 'and'. Fix in the spec: split p12 into two units, or move the primary-metric definition into the Concepts table and keep p12 on exposure.

results.quote: The table below compares the six designs: coarser units mean less interference and less power.
results.finding: The outliner needed two summaries (geographic experiments / the table comparing all designs). The closing sentence states the cross-design trade-off, a different idea from geographic experiments, because the spec's p32 controlling idea attaches the comparison table and its reading to the geographic paragraph. Fix in the spec: give the comparison table its own one-sentence unit (or attach it to p25, which already states the trade-off).

results.quote: Who decides: the Head of Data & ML owns the engine, the methods and the cluster maps;
results.finding: Unchanged from round 4: the outliner needed two summaries (decision ownership / metrics to watch). The paragraph has two labelled parts, and the spec's p52 controlling idea itself joins ownership and the estimate-to-rollout gap. Fix by splitting p52 into two units in the spec or recasting it around one idea.
Every unit aligns to a spec paragraph that supports S1-S5 directly or is a context, transition or synthesis unit of its section; no orphan paragraphs.

Every table, figure and quotation is framed: bump table -> p07 arithmetic; Figure 1/2/3/4/5 captions say what each shows; Concepts and interference tables carry 'why it matters' / 'what a naive test measures' columns; design table led by 'coarser units mean less interference and less power'; Holtz quotation glossed and tied to the bump test; Omnibus quote followed by the counsel point; eBay, OLX, Beasley and Adevinta sources each followed by what they imply; retest table -> p46; trade-off and vertical tables led by their reading.

Each declared boundary is expressed: 'A test at Veldmark ... shows such a transfer' (example), 'Explaining what went wrong ... needs a few precise terms' (sequence), 'The bump test is one case of interference' (elaboration), 'the right one depends on the mechanism' (problem_solution), 'Once the design fixes the unit' (sequence), 'where marketplace experimentation becomes governance' (emphasis), 'Every design, metric and review above needs platform support' (cause_effect), 'follows from the sections above' (conclusion_summary), 'Ignore these defaults' (contrast), 'prevents these failures' (problem_solution), 'These test whether those decisions hold' (cause_effect), and the conclusion's callback. p03 picks up interference only mid-paragraph ('changes that only looked like wins') and p12 does not refer back to the table explicitly; both judged acceptable, as in round 4.

Organising principle: both readers describe failure -> terms -> cause -> remedies -> metrics -> governance -> platform -> resolution -> reference, matching the spec's problem_solution flow with prerequisite_order and grouping, and both say the body keeps the roadmap's order. No section's position is unclear (Reader A calls Vertical Differences' place before Failure Modes 'a convention' but clear). The callout/body order mismatch that failed in round 4 no longer caused confusion for either reader. Not counted as failures: Veldmark, Hearthly, Valuo and Priya Raman used without gloss (A1, A3, A9, B1, B7, B10) are in audience.already_knows from earlier chapters, though a cheap role gloss for Priya Raman beside Ingrid's would remove a stumble both readers had; the 72-hour fraud restatement (A11, B9) is recorded under known_before_new.

results.draft_locus: Setting the Scene at Veldmark: The Bump That Ate Itself ¶4
results.quote: Contacts per bumped listing had fallen 31%.
results.finding: Both readers had to re-read to find the baseline of the 31% (year-over-year like the purchases, the February test, or pre-rollout). Name the comparison in the sentence. Reader A item 2: 'I could not tell whether the 31% uses the same comparison, the February test, or the pre-rollout level.'

results.draft_locus: Interference: Why Marketplace Tests Report the Wrong Number ¶2
results.quote: In their model, randomizing customers is unbiased when the market is demand-constrained
results.finding: Both readers needed two passes for the Johari et al. sentence: three findings, two parenthetical definitions and the definition of two-sided randomization in one sentence. Split it into two or three sentences. Reader A item 5: 'Three findings, two parenthetical definitions and a citation sit in one sentence. I needed two passes to hold it.'

results.draft_locus: Metrics: Liquidity First, Revenue Second, Both Watched ¶4
results.quote: That is why results are computed as a stream while a test runs
results.finding: Unchanged from round 4: 'That is why' presupposes streaming computation that the chapter only describes later (Adevinta, Kafka Streams). State it as a requirement ('so results must be computed as a stream while a test runs'). Reader A item 6: 'Nothing so far has said that results are computed as a stream.'

results.quote: The February bump test had neither, and the three cases below show what such a review must look for.
results.finding: Both readers could not map 'neither' to two things: the previous sentence names an owner plus registration and review of unit, metric and guardrails, and the bump test seems to have had an owner (Olivier). Say what it lacked ('was neither registered nor reviewed'). Reader A item 7: 'I could not tell which two things "neither" refers to.'

results.quote: it was designed under the experimentation standard Veldmark adopted in June 2027, after the bump test, which this chapter sets out after the architecture.
results.finding: Unchanged from round 4: the clause brings in a standard the reader has not seen and ends in a navigational aside, which made both readers pause. Shorten to a plain forward pointer in its own sentence, or let the scene's closing sentence (p10) announce that a standard and a retest follow. Reader A item 8: 'brings in a standard the reader has not seen yet.'

results.quote: Veldmark learned this the hard way: the September 2027 ranking-policy experiment in [[ranking]] and the bump-price retest in the next section could not share Tradeyard NL's clusters.
results.finding: Unchanged from round 4: this is the first mention that a retest exists, and 'learned this the hard way' promises a failure the chapter never shows (the retest simply moved to Belgium). Drop the 'hard way' framing and state the scheduling constraint plainly. Reader A item 8: 'I went looking for the hard lesson and did not find one.'

results.quote: Analyses should be restricted to exposed units (with the assignment as the randomization)
results.finding: Both readers could not tell what the parenthetical adds or qualifies. Say it plainly (e.g. 'while still comparing groups as assigned') or cut it. Reader A item 10: 'I could not work out what "with the assignment as the randomization" adds or qualifies.'

results.draft_locus: Concepts: What an Experiment Must Get Right ¶1 (table)
results.quote: Must match or be nested in the randomization unit; analyzing per buyer a test randomized per region understates uncertainty
results.finding: Reader A (item 4) found the analysis-unit row contradicting its own example: a buyer is nested in a region, so the rule seems to allow what the example forbids, and Failure Modes says 'Analysis unit finer than the randomization unit'. The direction is wrong: the randomization unit must match or be nested in the analysis unit (analyze at the randomization unit or coarser). One reader only, but a factual slip worth fixing.

results.quote: Hearthly's pricing hint therefore goes live in Lyon and Bordeaux on 22 November 2027
results.finding: Reader A (item 9) noticed the present-tense 'goes live' on a 2027 date among past-tense 2027 narrative (e.g. 'withdrew it on Monday 6 December 2027'). One reader only.

The 72-hour fraud restatement is not in audience.already_knows (which lists the qualified contact and governed metrics, not the restatement) and the chapter never says what it is. Both flow readers reported it as unexplained (A item 11, B item 9). Add a short gloss (e.g. 'contacts later found to be fraud are removed within 72 hours').

The introduction opens on a direct statement of the SUTVA assumption, illustrates it with marketplace examples, states the stakes (wrong sign), places the chapter and gives a roadmap; none of the weak patterns.

The conclusion does not open with 'in conclusion', adds no new idea or evidence, and does not end on a restated thesis alone: it diagnoses the bump test and the retest together and ends on a hand-off.

p54 joins seller assignment, the unwatched control and the missing review into one diagnosis and the retest's cluster unit, guardrails and review into one remedy, which no single section states, and gives the so-what: experiments decide what ships, so a user-only platform can commit the business to the wrong sign, revealed by the estimate-to-rollout gap.
'seller assignment broke the assumption this chapter opened with' returns to the SUTVA assumption of p01 and to the February bump test, as callback.to requires.

The cold reader predicted the twelve sections in the body's order, the four themes (four contracts, randomization unit by mechanism, guardrails for the untested side, governance of price and ranking tests), the evidence kinds (published research, Adevinta/eBay/OLX/Zalando, EU consumer law, the fictional Veldmark) and the tone. It could not name the specific papers (Johari, Holtz, Kohavi) because the intro says only 'published marketplace research'; the kind of evidence is predicted, which is what the check asks.

The cold reader explained interference as a transfer between treated and control sellers competing for first-page time, cited the control's -9% contacts per bump as the tell and congestion at rollout, and designed a retest with region x category clusters, governed metrics, control-trend and congestion guardrails, pre-registration and review by monetization and regulatory owners, and wider intervals as the price of the right sign: matches the expected answer.
